rationale.product_understanding: analysis.md:22-42 separates facts, design assumptions and unknowns (seat-on-send, Admin copy, activation event), and app.js:14-26 keeps Admin and Member copy to the brief's rules. Framing the batch-role model as a product assumption as well as a trade-off would strengthen it.
rationale.ux_reasoning: analysis.md:46-58 and 92-105 make the project form the hero, put role capabilities in the rail from step one and keep Skip for now persistent; app.js:365-410 makes Go to workspace primary. Adding a direct Open project action on success would remove the last extra hop.
rationale.design_judgment: analysis.md:162-172 gives nine explicit decisions with costs, including deliberately omitting a wizard and explaining roles twice. The one-role-per-batch invite is justified at line 131, but costing the mixed-role case would complete the reasoning.
rationale.visual_hierarchy: desktop-rail-roles.png and desktop-form.png show a strong dark-rail plus serif-heading composition with clear grouping. mobile-controls-overlap.png shows the floating Prototype controls bar covering the Description label and its Optional marker; collapsing the demo controls on narrow screens would raise this.
rationale.interaction_completeness: app.js:413-550 renders validation, loading and failure states, while app.js:794-857 handles submission, failure and retry; a seat-limit state and guarded localStorage persistence cover resume. The failure path is all-or-nothing and retries the whole list, with no per-address partial-success state; adding that would raise this.
rationale.accessibility_responsiveness: checks.json reports 0 axe violations, 0 unnamed controls and no horizontal overflow at both viewports, and analysis.md:186-193 documents labels, aria-invalid, focus movement and live regions. Fixing the mobile demo-bar overlap would remove the remaining viewport concern.
rationale.implementation_quality: app.js is dependency-free and organised by view with escaping and guarded localStorage; checks.json shows no console or page errors. The batch-only invite model and all-or-nothing failure are deliberate but limit future extension.

Invite rows are capped at 3 per batch although Starter leaves 4 seats (app.js:11,335-336).
Role card claims Admin 'Manages workspace settings' without flagging the inference (app.js:179; analysis.md:78).

comparison: Candidate A is leaner: role education and plan context sit beside the only required field, with no extra welcome screen, and its trade-off write-up is the stronger of the two. Candidate B renders more cleanly on mobile and recovers partial invitation failures per row, but its welcome screen repeats the rail, its 3-invite batch cap adds friction the brief does not require, and its Admin role copy is not grounded.
limitations: Only initial screenshots were available, so invite, success, failure, limit and paused renders could not be inspected. The in-page check harnesses and transcripts claimed by Candidate A were not supplied, and backend, email-delivery and screen-reader behavior could not be verified.
